about: Where this SDK, replaying a shared recording from rius-semconv, produces something other than the recording's stored expected result. For the families both SDKs cover the expected result is the Python SDK's, so these are the places the two SDKs disagree. Each entry is reviewed and says why. tests/conformance.test.ts fails on any difference not listed here and on a listed one that no longer occurs, so fixing a difference means deleting its entry in the same change. `key` is an attribute key, or one of `events`, `status`, `name`, `kind`; "*" covers every difference in the family.

differences.reason: LiteLLM is Python-only, so this SDK never sees these spans live and does not move a LiteLLM wrapper's usage. The Python SDK, the reference here, moves the completion span's usage to rius.aggregated_usage.* when its OpenAI child recorded the same call.

The stored expected results record tool definitions in the provider's own shape (OpenAI's nested function, Anthropic's input_schema, the AI SDK's inputSchema and provider-defined tools). This normalizer now records them in the conventions' function-tool shape, {type: function, name, description, parameters}, which the conventions' schema requires for a function tool, and prefixes a built-in tool's type with its provider. The expected results are regenerated in rius-semconv once the change is released, and this entry goes in that re-sync.
